tab on Android: 1.Verify Group Similar Faces Status: Open Google Photos, tap your Profile icon > Photos settings > Preferences > Group similar faces, and ensure Face grouping is turned ON. 2.Re-label Unnamed Faces: Go to the Collections (or Search) tab, select People & pets, tap a face, choose Add a name at the top, and type the person's name. 3.Search via the Main Search Bar: Instead of searching directly inside the People tab, tap the main Search icon at the bottom, type the assigned name in the search bar, and press enter. 4.Clear App Cache and Updates: Go to Settings > Apps > Photos > Storage & cache, tap Clear Cache, or go to the three dots at the top right and select Uninstall updates to reset glitched features.

title: Indexing issue

replies: > Google Photos search is broken on this account. The same Google Photos app on the same iPhone can search objects such as

correctly when I switch to another Google account. On this account, only location searches and People & Pets work. Searches for simple objects return no results. 1 have already deleted and reinstalled Google Photos, and my entire photo library is backed up. Please check/rebuild the visual search index for this account.

Hi Rapidm3, Because you’ve already narrowed this down to an account-specific issue - by successfully searching on a different account using the same app and device - you can skip standard troubleshooting like re-installing the app or clearing local data. Here are a few key points regarding how indexing works on Google Photos and what you can do next: Account Indexing & Product Experts No Manual Indexing Tool: Neither forum Product Experts nor Google Support agents have a mechanism to manually trigger or rebuild an account's visual search index. Indexing is handled entirely by automated backend servers. Server-Side Delays/Glitches: Account-level search failures for general terms/objects (while metadata-based searches like Locations and labeled People/Pets still work) usually point to a serv
>photos.google.com on a computer or desktop browser while logged into the affected account. Try searching for

there. If web search also fails, it confirms the issue is 100% on the backend server index rather than an app syncing glitch. Send Direct In-App Feedback (Crucial Step): Since Product Experts cannot trigger a rebuild, the best way to flag an indexing failure on your specific account directly to the engineering team is via the feedback tool. In the Google Photos iOS app, tap your Profile Icon in the top right > Help & feedback > Send feedback . Briefly describe the issue (e.g.,

). Be sure to leave the box checked to include system logs and screenshots. This provides backend engineers with the account diagnostics needed to investigate indexing stalls. While sending feedback won't generate a direct email response from engineers, it routes your account diagnostic data to the team monitoring backend indexing issues. In many cases, these account-level index stalls resolve automatically once a background maintenance cycle runs on the server. Hope this helps clarify what's happening! Best regards, Doug (Volunteer Google Photos user)

You can now seamlessly integrate both classic and Ask Photos search experiences which makes it easier to shift between them based on your query. To find a specific moment or ask a complex question, Google Photos helps you browse memories in a more descriptive way. You can say, “What did I eat on my trip to Barcelona?” or “Photos that would make great phone backgrounds.” What’s changing? Classic search remains fast, but with a powerful new layer of information when you need it. Now, you can switch between Ask Photos and the classic search experience at any time. Use Ask Photos If you turn on Ask Photos: The app decides whether your search is best answered with Ask Photos or a classic search experience. To switch between results, at the top of your search results, toggle back and forth. If you haven’t turned on Ask Photos: You can still perform your standard searches as usual. At the top of your results, you may find a toggle to enable Ask Photos. When you toggle on, it’ll lead you to the onboarding and opt-in flow. <a href=

We appreciate your continued feedback as we work to improve the search experience and help you find your most important memories. <a href=

title: I don't want my photos on my Google account
text: I don't want my photos attached to my Google account

replies: Good day OTIS POWERS! Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum! To completely decouple your photos from your Google account—without accidentally wiping out the local photos stored on your phone's internal storage—you need to execute a specific order of operations. If you just hit

inside the Google Photos app while it is connected, it will delete the files off your phone, too. Follow these steps to safely sever the link and purge your cloud library. Step 1: Turn Off Cloud Backup Immediately First, make sure your phone stops uploading new photos to your Google storage. Open the Google Photos app. Tap your Profile Icon in the top-right corner. Tap Photos settings (the gear icon) > Backup . Toggle the Backup switch to OFF . Step 2: Use

Google includes an automated feature on Android specifically designed to wipe your account's cloud copy while keeping 100% of the photos on your physical phone. While still inside the Backup settings screen: Scroll down to the bottom and look for Undo backup . Check the confirmation box acknowledging that backed-up files will be removed from your Google Account. Tap Delete Google Photos backup . What this does: This triggers a server-side wipe that clears your Google cloud storage while leaving every picture sitting safely on your phone's internal storage. Step 3: Unlink Your Google Account from the Gallery To prevent the app from continuing to display your Google profile or prompting you to sync, you can switch the app to operate purely as an offline device gallery. Open Google Photos app

>photos.google.com . Sign in with your Google account credentials. Check your library. If any old photos remain, you can select them and hit the Trash icon to delete them directly from the web browser. Empty the Trash in the left-hand menu to instantly reclaim your account storage space. (Because you set the app on your phone to
in Step 3, deleting files on the website will have zero effect on your Android phone's local camera roll). Hope this helps. Regards, Lex

replies: Hi Hi Marvin D, Welcome to Google Photos Help Community. Google Photos search does much more than just look at caption, filenames or timestamps. It analyzes descriptions, creation time, metadata, and the actual contents of the photo. For example, if a photo contains a mountain, a river, and other natural elements in the same frame, Google’s AI can identify all of those details and make them searchable later. This type of analysis requires a lot of processing power, which is why Google performs it on its servers rather than on the phone itself. That’s also why the photos need to be uploaded to Google Photos for the full search functionality to work. text: Dear Google Photos Team, I am a regular user of Google Photos, and while I love the cloud backup feature, managing a large number of files has become very difficult due to the lack of basic file-management tools. I strongly request you to add the following features to make the app more user-friendly: 1. Add

replies: Options in Main Gallery Right now, there is no way to organize files other than by date. Please add a

menu with these options: Newest date first / Oldest date first Largest size first / Smallest size first (Crucial for clearing up storage space easily) Name A to Z / Name Z to A 2. Improve the Grid View (Show Titles & 3-Dot Menu) In the default Grid View, we can only see the picture or video preview. We cannot see the filename or title unless we click the file and swipe up. Request: Please add an option to show the file title/name directly under each photo or video thumbnail in the grid. Request: Place a small 3-dot menu icon next to the title so we can check details, delete, or share directly from the main screen without opening the file. 3. Introduce a

Option (Like Google Drive / File Manager) For users who manage a lot of study videos, official documents, or specific image series, a Grid View is not enough. We desperately need a List View toggle button at the top. The layout should look like this: Left side: A small square image/video thumbnail. Middle portion: The full filename/title and date. Right side: A 3-dot options menu for quick action. Implementing these features will bridge the gap between a simple gallery and a powerful media manager, making Google Photos the ultimate app for everyone. Thank you, A Hopeful Google Photos User.

Touch and hold the photo or video you want to restore. If the photo or video isn’t in your trash, it may be permanently deleted. At the bottom, tap Restore . title: Search blocks terms to hide private photos. Manual hunting is a risk
text: Google Photos is great at finding pictures of my dog or a specific vacation. It falls short on privacy management. We need a way to search for sensitive images so we can move them to the Locked Folder or delete them. Right now, if I accidentally leave a private photo in my main feed, I have to scroll through thousands of thumbnails to find it. That's a major privacy risk when I'm showing someone a picture on my phone. It creates the exact situation the Locked Folder is supposed to prevent. Blocking these searches makes it harder to manage our data without actually increasing security. Give us the tools to handle our own privacy properly. The search feature in Google Photos is missing a critical privacy tool. It finds sunsets in seconds. It fails to find sensitive photos I accidentally left in my main feed. This makes the Locked Folder less effective. If I can't find the images to move them, they stay exposed in my history. Blocking these keywords is just a hurdle for people trying to be responsible with their data. Allow these searches so we can clean up our libraries.

title: Why I cant see lock folder on google photos

replies: Hi Geet, Welcome to the Google Photos Help Community. Here are some information I can share about Locked Folder in Google Photos. Locked Folder is protected by your device’s screen lock in the Google Photos app. If you enable backup for Locked Folder , you can access Locked Folder from other devices when you’re signed in with your Google Account Items in Locked Folder that you don’t back up are stored only on your device . You won’t be able to see these items from other devices that you’re signed in to with Locked Folder. You’ll lose items in Locked Folder that haven’t been backed up if: You uninstall the Photos app You delete the Photos app data Your device is damaged or lost IMPORTANT: BACKED UP OR NOT BACKED UP, if the Photos are deleted from Locked Folder, then the deletion is permanen

The issue you’re seeing is caused by app performance problems on large libraries , not a bug with your Pixel specifically. Google Photos can struggle to load many photos at once, which causes scrolling to stutter or crash. Even with backups on Drive, the app still has to load thumbnails and metadata locally. On newer devices like the Pixel 10, higher-resolution screens and larger libraries can make this more noticeable compared to older devices. Closing and reopening the app temporarily fixes it because it clears memory, but there’s no permanent fix inside the app. Reducing the number of photos loading at once (for example, by switching to a specific album or searching for a date) can make scrolling smoother. replies: Welcome to the Google Photos Support community! Hi there, If you want to find the location where a photo was taken , please follow these steps: Open the Google Photos app on your Android device. Select the photo you want to check. Tap the “Info (i)” icon or swipe up on the photo. You’ll see the location details (like city or map view) if the photo has location data. Note: If no location appears, it means the photo doesn’t have location info saved. This can happen if Location was turned off on your device’s camera when the picture was taken. You can also manually add a location : Tap “Add a location” (if available) and select the correct one. For more details, visit the official guide: <a href=
>View and edit photo locations in Google Photos Glad I could help. If you're satisfied, please hit 👍. With regards, Sabbir Ahmed

Hi JohnnyR4181, Welcome to the Google Photos Help Community. If you're trying to find the original source of a video you've downloaded , here are a few steps you can try. Please note, Google Photos itself doesn’t track or display the original source URL if the video was uploaded or saved from elsewhere. Here are a few suggestions: 1. Check Video Metadata (EXIF data) On a computer, right-click the video file > Properties (Windows) or Get Info (Mac). This may show information like creation date, device used , or even software used to edit or export it. Unfortunately, most downloaded videos (especially from social media or messaging apps) often have stripped metadata. 2. Look in Google Photos Info Panel If the video is stored in Google Photos: Open the video. Click the

(info) icon. You’ll see the date , location (if available) , and device info — but not the original source URL if it was downloaded externally and uploaded to Photos. 3. Try Reverse Video Search (Workaround) Reverse video search isn’t natively supported in Google. A workaround is to: Take a screenshot of a clear frame from the video. Use Google Lens or Google Images reverse search. This might help identify the source if the video is popular or public. 4. Check Browser or App Download History If you downloaded the video via a browser: Check your browser download history or URL history . If it came from an app (like WhatsApp, Facebook, etc.), check the chat or post it came from. Hi Jenny Goodhand, Welcome to the Google Photos Help Community. If you're seeing Motion Photos play automatically when viewing your pictures in Google Photos and want to stop that from happening, you're not alone — this is a common question. Here’s how you can control that behaviour: 📌 To stop Motion Photos from playing automatically: Open the <a href=

>Google Photos app on your phone (Android or iOS). Tap your profile picture (top right corner). Go to Photos settings . Tap on Preferences > Motion photos (or Playback settings on some devices). Turn off the toggle for “Automatically play Motion Photos.” Once disabled, your Motion Photos will show only the still image unless you tap to view the motion manually. What are Motion Photos? Motion Photos are short clips captured before and after you press the shutter — kind of like a mini video around your photo. They're supported on many Android devices (especially Pixel phones), and Google Photos plays them by default unless you turn it off. Let me know if the steps look different on your device — sometimes the menu names can vary slightly depending on your phone model or Google Photos version

replies: Dear Dezeree, Thank you for reaching out in the Google Photos Help Community. I understand that you're unable to see your photos after switching to your second Google account. Confirm You're Signed In to the Correct Account Sometimes we switch between accounts on a device, and the photos are simply in a different Google account. Open the Google Photos app (or go to <a href=
>photos.google.com ) Tap your profile icon (top right) Make sure you're signed into the correct account where your photos were originally backed up. If not, tap

and log in to the correct one. 2. Check Backup Settings on the Original Device If you're expecting photos to appear in your second account , they must have been backed up to that account from the device. On your device, open Google Photos > Tap profile icon > Photos settings > <a href=

Photos May Not Be Backed Up Yet If the photos are only stored on your device and haven’t been backed up, they will not appear in the second account. You can manually back them up to the intended account by: Signing into the second account in Google Photos Enabling backup for that account Selecting the photos you want to upload Hope this helps. Have a wonderful day. Best regards, Prudhvi

You can nudge the system along by continuing to take photos of people / pets you care about so the system learns who are important subjects in your photos. title: Face Grouping issues
text: Hello! I have been experiencing a serious worsening in the Google Photos

replies: feature since late December 2025. I would like to know if I am the only one. I successfully used the

feature from 2020 until December 2025. For over five years: - I tagged faces identified by the system, added faces, and removed faces without ever encountering a problem. - The faces—numbering between 800 and 1,000—were neatly sorted by photo count. - Furthermore, three or four times a year, there was a nice database update; it was great, for example, to see new children move up the list as more photos of them were added. Suddenly, in mid-December 2025, the system started throwing errors preventing me from editing faces. - Whether using the app or a web browser, if I try to link an unrecognized face to an existing tagged face, or create a new face, or remove a misidentified face, I either get a

error message or nothing happens at all. - Additionally, database management has significantly worsened: faces with only one or two photos are consistently appearing at the top of the list, while faces with hundreds of photos are at the bottom. - Database updates—if they happen at all—are extremely rare. Support recommends starting from scratch by disabling and re-enabling the face grouping feature. I’ve tried twice, but every time—after a promising start and reaching around 800 faces—the problem recurs, bringing everything to a halt. Furthermore, since late September 2026, no faces are being recognized in new photos uploaded via any method (smartphone or web). Essentially, we’ve gone from a great, well-functioning system—one that convinced me to sign up for a

subscription to manage my photos—to a system that performs poorly, suddenly stalls without providing any diagnostic info, and seems determined to drive me toward looking for other services on the market. Support is always quick and polite, but they lack the possibility to intervene effectively. They suggest some good photo management tips and suggest starting from scratch by disabling and re-enabling the feature, but—as I mentioned—nothing works. It seems there are no diagnostic tools to pinpoint the exact issue, nor any way to force an update. I’m curious to know if anyone else has experienced this problem and, if so, if there are any practical suggestions. Thanks, everyone.

title: Google Photos Face Groups Disappeared After Accidentally Disabling “Group Similar Faces”
text: I accidentally turned off the “Group similar faces” option in Google Photos. Immediately after disabling this setting, all of my previously created face groups disappeared. I turned the “Group similar faces” option back on right away, but my existing face groups have not returned. This is very concerning because I had many important face groups organized in Google Photos. I did not intend to delete or reset any of this data; I only accidentally turned the setting off and then enabled it again immediately. Please check my account and restore my previously created face groups and associated face-grouping data if possible. I would greatly appreciate it if the existing groups could be recovered rather than having to recreate or wait for everything to be processed again. Thank you for your help.

replies: Good day Yash! Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum! When you turn off Group similar faces in Google Photos, Google's system automatically purges the face grouping index, face models, and custom labels assigned to those face groups from your account on their backend servers. Unfortunately, because this deletion is designed as a privacy reset feature, there is no undo button or backup store to immediately restore your old face groups or custom names. However, turning the setting back on has initialized a fresh scan of your entire photo library. What Happens Now & How to Speed Up Recovery Automatic Re-Scanning in the Background: Now that Group similar faces is toggled back ON, Google's AI facial recognition algorithms will re-scan all the photos in your cloud library. Timelin

) were cleared during the toggle reset. You will need to type in the name labels once the face clusters begin repopulating. Check Force Indexing via Web: Open a browser on a desktop or phone and navigate to <a href=

>photos.google.com/people . The web interface often displays newly generated face clusters faster than the mobile app, which relies on local cache updates. Best Practices to Assist the Server Rescan Keep the Google Photos app updated on your Android phone. Ensure your phone is connected to unmetered Wi-Fi and left charging overnight so cloud sync and server-side indexing run unimpeded. Avoid toggling the setting off and on repeatedly, as every toggle forces the server to wipe the queue and start scanning from 0% again. Send Feedback to Request a Confirmation Prompt (a suggestion) Speaking as a fellow Google Photos user here, since accidental toggling wipes significant data instantly, you can try submitting feature feedback directly to the Google Photos product team to request a confirmatio
) to prevent this for yourself and other users in the future. How to Send Feedback in Google Photos: Open the Google Photos app on your Android phone (or go to <a href=
>photos.google.com on a browser). Tap your Profile Icon in the top right corner. Tap Help & feedback --> Send feedback (or Send feedback to Google ). Enter your suggestion clearly. For example:
(Optional) Keep the Include screenshot and logs option checked so the engineers can see the UI context. Tap Send (the paper airplane icon). Regards, Lex

replies: Hi Samstone, Welcome to the Google Photos Help Community! It is frustrating when face grouping remains blank after toggling the setting on and off . Turning Face Grouping off and back on resets the face indexing process on Google's cloud servers, forcing the system to rescan your library from scratch. Here is a breakdown of why this happens and how to troubleshoot the issue: 1. Account Verification (Work or School Accounts) If you use multiple Google Accounts on your iPhone, ensure you are signed into your primary personal account . Workspace Restrictions: Managed Google Workspace accounts (work or school) often have administrator policies that disable AI features like Face Grouping . Check Active Account: Tap your Profile Circle in the top right corner of the Google Photos app to verify y

>photos.google.com on a computer or browser . Click Explore or People & Pets to see if faces appear . If face groups show up on the web but not in your iOS app, reset the app's local sync connection : Open Google Photos on your iPhone . Tap your Profile Picture > tap the down arrow next to your name > select Use without an account . Force-close the app, wait 10 seconds, reopen it, and sign back into your Google Account . Avoid toggling the Face Grouping setting off again, as every toggle clears server progress and restarts the entire queue from the beginning . Scroll to the bottom to check if Google created new, unlabeled face clusters for those people instead of matching them to existing ones. Labeling these new groups with the exact same name will prompt Google to merge them. Review

Suggestions: Open a primary person's profile in People & pets, tap the three dots in the top-right corner, and select Improve results or Review same person suggestions. Confirming matches trains the AI server model for your account. Verify Hidden Faces: Go to People & pets, tap the three dots, and choose Hide & show people. Ensure the missing face profiles were not accidentally hidden. Check the Web Interface: Log in to <a href=

>photos.google.com on a computer web browser and check Settings > Group similar faces. Verify that Face grouping is turned ON and not restricted on the account settings level. Do NOT Toggle Face Grouping Off/On: Avoid turning
off and back on in settings. Doing so will completely wipe all your custom face groups and face history permanently.

replies: Hi David, This is a peer-to-peer volunteer community forum, so we don't have access to your account or direct influence over engineering decisions. However, your feedback highlights an important pain point for power users and business accounts managing large photo libraries. title: Feature Request: Improve Face Detection and Face Grouping
text: Google Photos should improve its face detection and face grouping system. When I upload/import photos to Google Photos, some photos contain clearly visible faces, but Google Photos does not detect those faces or add them to the appropriate People & Pets / Face Groups. Because of this, many imported photos cannot be found by searching for a particular person. The feature should work as follows: Detect faces more accurately Google Photos should scan all uploaded and imported photos for faces, including older photos. Automatically add detected faces to Face Groups If a face is detected, the photo should be included in the appropriate person's face group. Rescan existing photos Google Photos should provide an option such as “Scan/Rescan for Faces” so users can rescan their entire library when some faces were missed during the original upload. Handle different photo qualities Face detection should work as much as possible with old, low-resolution, blurry, dark, side-profile, or partially visible faces. Allow users to manually identify a face If Google Photos fails to detect or group a face automatically, users should be able to select the face in a photo and manually assign it to an existing person. Improve imported-photo processing Imported photos should go through the same face-detection and grouping process as newly uploaded photos. Make all photos searchable by person Once a person is identified, all photos containing that person should appear in their Face Group, regardless of when or how the photo was uploaded. Example Suppose I have 10,000 old photos and many of them contain my family members. After importing them into Google Photos, only some photos are added to the correct Face Groups, while many photos containing clearly visible faces are not recognized. Google Photos should provide a full-library face rescan that detects these missing faces and automatically adds them to the correct Face Groups. This would make it much easier to find imported and older photos by searching for a specific person.

title: All of the names of people I added to my photos are no longer there. I checked and face groups is on
text: I went in and added names to everyone in Google photos and so I can search for people and now there are no names. And face groups is on. If I accidentally turned it off then on again will it delete them all? And is there a way to restore all the names?

replies: Good day Tisha! Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum! Yes, unfortunately: if Face Grouping was turned off and then turned back on, Google Photos automatically wipes all custom name labels you created. When Face Grouping is toggled off—even accidentally for a few seconds—Google treats it as a privacy reset and deletes all the biometric face clusters and associated name labels stored on their servers. Toggling it back on forces the AI to start from scratch, re-scanning your photos to cluster faces together into unnamed groups. Is There a Way to Automatically Restore the Names? Regrettably, there is no

title: Few of my photos are not face tagged
text: I have enabled auto photo upload in album if it sees a particular person in it. But lately seeing that the person face is not getting detected when photos are shot in portait mode with 50mp default camera

replies: High-resolution (50MP) portrait mode images can overwhelm the cloud-based AI that powers Google Photos face tagging. The ultra-high pixel density and heavy background blur make it difficult for the scanner to isolate facial geometry, leading to missed detections. To fix this and trigger your auto-upload albums, take the following steps: 1. Force a Manual Tag (Highly Effective) Manually assigning a face to a photo forces the Google Photos cloud engine to recognize similar facial geometry in your other uploads. Open the untagged photo in the Google Photos App. Swipe up or tap the three-dot menu to open the details panel. Look for People and tap the Edit (pencil) icon. Tap the Add (
) button over the unrecognized face and select or create the person's name. 2. Make a

Editing a photo forces the server to re-index the file, often prompting the AI to run a fresh scan on the image. Open the unlinked photo in the Google Photos app. Tap the Info/Details icon and add a simple caption (e.g.,

). 3. Clear the App Cache Temporary local glitches can prevent your phone from submitting indexing requests. Go to your device's Settings > Apps > Google Photos > Storage. Tap Clear Cache (Do not clear storage or data). 4. Optimize Background Scanning Face grouping requires background processing on Google's servers, which only kicks in under specific conditions. Connect your phone to Wi-Fi, plug it into a charger, and leave the screen off.

Manually Label Your Face: If Google has grouped photos of you but hasn't named the face, tap the unrecognized face in your

Tap on one of the face groups that belongs to the person. At the top of the screen, tap Add name (or tap the existing name if you want to edit it) and type their name. Go back and tap on the second, separate face group of the same person. Tap Add name and type the exact same name you used for the first group. Google Photos will ask you a prompt along the lines of
. Tap Yes or Merge . It might take a few moments for all the photos to sync up into the single folder, but they will now be combined. For more detailed management options, you can check the <a href=

title: New photos not being scans for Faces
text: Face recognition is completely stuck at July 2025. Brand new photos are seemingly not being scanned for faces. I've left it for a week, and photos all the way back to ~July 2025 have no face groups. Photos taken before ~July 2025 have been successfully scanned. Thank you for any help provided.

replies: If your face recognition has completely stalled for new uploads, the cloud servers likely paused processing your facial models. You can manually
the scanner and clear stuck files to get it back up and running. Remember you want to be on good Wi-Fi and full battery. Try these steps to wake up the scanner: DO NOT toggle

off and on: Doing so can permanently delete all your existing face groupings and trained AI data. Clear App Cache: Go to your device Settings > Apps > Google Photos > Storage and tap Clear Cache (do not clear storage/data). Nudge with a Caption: Open one of your recent, un-scanned photos, swipe up to the info panel, and add a quick text caption (e.g.,
). This forces the server to update the image's metadata and re-index the file. Force a Background Sync: Ensure the app has

battery usage permissions so the OS doesn't kill the background process. Plug your phone into a charger overnight, connect to Wi-Fi, and open the Google Photos app. Manually Tag a Face: Locate a clearly visible face in a recent photo, tap the three-dot menu, and manually assign a name to it. Doing so gives the algorithm training data and encourages it to scan nearby un-tagged photos. If these steps don't yield results within 72 hours, you can submit a manual report using the Send Feedback tool inside the app's Help menu so Google's engineers can reset the sync for your specific account

title: Accessing photos from Picasa 3
text: Airmor isn't getting all photos on my android phone. Doesn't pull Picasa 3 photo albums.

replies: Hey! Be welcome to Googlee Photos Community! AirMore cannot pull Picasa 3 web albums because Google completely retired Picasa and its underlying APIs. AirMore relies on reading local folders stored directly on your phone's storage or active gallery databases, but Picasa Web Albums no longer exist as a syncable service. Why AirMore Doesn't Show Picasa Albums Picasa API Deprecation: Google shut down the Picasa Web Albums Data API that third-party file transfer tools (like AirMore) used to access cloud albums. Local Storage vs. Cloud: The Picasa 3 desktop application kept pictures in folders on a computer, not inside the phone's physical memory. AirMore can only scan and transfer media that is physically saved on your Android device's internal storage or SD card. How to Access & Move Your Pho

>Google Photos or the Google Photos app on your Android phone using the same Google Account you used for Picasa. Download Photos to Local Storage: If you want AirMore to see these photos, they must be saved locally on your phone's storage. In the Google Photos app, select the photos or albums you need, tap the three-dot menu icon , and tap Download (or Save to Device ). Transfer PC Folders directly: If the Picasa 3 photos were saved locally on your computer, connect your computer and phone to AirMore via Wi-Fi. Upload the image folders directly from your PC's Pictures directory to your phone's internal memory using the AirMore web interface on your desktop browser. I'd hope had been helpful! replies: Hello, In general it is not a good idea to turn face grouping off and back on to try to force it to refresh. Plug in your device to charge. Open the Google Photos app

>. Let your device sit overnight. Make sure your device is plugged in and connected to Wi-Fi all night. Tips: If only some of your photos appear in face groups, try the process again for one more night. title: Feature Request: Fixing Face Tagging Bottlenecks & Improving the
text: UI Flaws

replies: Hi everyone, I am writing to share some feedback regarding a noticeable performance decline in the automated Face Detection/Grouping features over the past year, alongside a few constructive feature suggestions to help solve the workflow bottlenecks this causes. Currently, when the face detection fails to register a face, the workflow for fixing and reporting it is highly repetitive and structurally flawed. I would love to get the thoughts of the Community Product Experts and see if these suggestions can be flagged for the development team: 1. True Manual Face Tagging (Independent Pin Dropping): Currently, we can only edit a face if the algorithm detects a shadow or shape first. We need an option to manually drop a tag anywhere on a photo/video when the scanner misses it entirely. 2. Bulk

Telemetry Checkbox: Currently, because you have to swipe up the info panel to access the feedback button, the auto-generated screenshot frequently cuts off the top of the photo, or misses errors that happen later in a video's runtime. Google should add a simple checkbox stating

so engineers know the telemetry is cropped, allowing them to track the rate of this interface issue. As someone with a large library who relies heavily on these organization tools for media creations, the current lack of manual override and batch-management options adds massive friction. I welcome any insight or escalation from the Product Experts here to pass these UI improvements along to the team. Thanks in advance!

About Face grouping: you are absolutely right that correcting errors or adding missing faces is a pain. The option to add a shape already existed in Picasa years ago, as well as bulk allocation. And when you live in Europe it's worse: you can't even correct or add at all. I have less experience with sending feedback, but these suggestions seem also interesting. But I am afraid that I have to disappoint you: PE's can escalate bugs, but we are told that requests for new or improved features must be sent via Feedback.

replies: Good day Travel Khalife! Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum! 1. Check if the Update Accidnetally Toggled the Setting Off Major app overhauls occasionally reset privacy preferences to default. If the update switched face grouping off, it hides the entire collection from the interface. Open Google Photos and tap your Profile Icon in the top right. Go to Photos settings > Preferences > Memories (or Privacy depending on the exact update version). Look for Face Groups (or Group similar faces ). Crucial: Ensure it is toggled ON . ⚠️ If it is already ON, do not toggle it off and on again. Turning it off actively commands Google's servers to permanently delete your entire face model history, forcing a multi-week re-scan from scratch. Leave it on. 2. Force-Refresh the

UI Cache Since the data tier upgrade and app update happened simultaneously, the app's local memory is bloated with old configuration parameters. Clearing the app's cache forces the interface to re-fetch layout tiles from your account. Go to your phone's main Settings > Apps > Google Photos . Tap Storage & cache . Select Clear Cache (this will not touch your actual photos). Tap Force Stop to shut down the app entirely. Reopen Google Photos while connected to a strong Wi-Fi network and wait a minute for the Collections tab to ping the server. 3. Check the

Overflow Sometimes a structural layout update automatically collapses face groupings into the hidden items directory. In the Google Photos app, tap the Search tab (or check the top of the Collections tab). Next to the blank People section, tap View All . Tap the three vertical dots (⋮) in the upper-right corner and select Show & hide faces . Check to see if your entire collection was mistakenly flagged as

during the software update layout merge. If they are grayed out, simply tap them to unhide them. 4. Leverage Your 2TB Google One Status Because you just upgraded to a 2TB Google One tier , you have priority access to dedicated Google technicians who can look at your server logs. If the collection doesn't reappear within 24 hours of clearing your cache, it means your account tier migration stalled on the backend. title: The 'People' section was accidentally deleted by me but now even after turning it on it doesn't show
text: I accidentally disabled the “Group similar faces” / “Face grouping” feature in Google Photos around a month ago due to a confusing pop-up while rapidly switching between multiple Google accounts in the app. The pop-up appeared after I had already switched accounts, so I mistakenly believed the prompt belonged to another account and disabled it immediately. After realizing the issue, I re-enabled “Group similar faces” almost immediately (within minutes). However, since then: The “People & Pets” section has never properly returned. Only empty placeholder silhouettes appear. Automatic face clustering is not working. Google Photos detects faces manually, but it does not automatically group similar faces together anymore. If I manually assign a face to a person, it only adds that single image and does not scan or associate other photos of the same person. No “same person?” suggestions appear anymore. No automatic grouping behavior is occurring even after approximately one month. Important context: This account has over 10 years of photo history and previously had a very extensive and well-trained People & Pets library with manually labeled individuals and years of face-confirmation training. The feature worked perfectly before it was disabled. The issue persists across app restarts and after ensuring “Group similar faces” is enabled again. The People section itself was initially completely missing, but later returned only as empty placeholders without functioning grouping behavior. Things I have already tried: Re-enabling “Group similar faces” Waiting several weeks Keeping the device charging on Wi-Fi overnight Opening and scrolling through many face-heavy photos Updating Google Photos Clearing app cache Checking Google Photos web version At this point it appears the face clustering/indexing system may be stuck or failed to rebuild correctly after disabling and re-enabling the feature. I would like to know: Whether the original People & Pets model/data is permanently deleted after disabling the feature Whether automatic regrouping is expected to return Whether my account’s face-indexing pipeline may be stuck Whether there is any way for Google support to re-trigger or repair the clustering/indexing process Thank you.

Make sure Face Grouping is enabled by following these steps: On your iPhone or iPad, open the Google Photos app
>. Sign in to your Google Account. At the top right, tap your Account profile photo or Initials. Tap Google Photos settings

> Privacy. Turn Face Groups on. Since you have a large number of photos, the grouping process may take additional time. To help improve face recognition, try creating a few albums for specific people. This can help trigger the face grouping algorithm to detect and create new face groups more effectively. title: mixing people up
text: whenever i’m looking for someone i can never find them and it turns out they were put undder someone else’s face. why doesn’t google photos ask and make sure before it puts someone it’s not sure of?

replies: Hello Face grouping is dynamic and some errors can occur. Google does sometimes ask you to confirm faces to make sure it is making the correct match. You may sometimes see the prompt at the bottom of the screen when you open the Face groupings. It will say something like

and show two thumbnail icons and you can select the green checkmark or red x to indicate your choice. This doesn't always show in a face grouping, but pay attention when it pops up to help train things. You can open a face grouping and if you find a face that shouldn't be there, you can select it and remove it from the group. Be careful as this cannot be undone. This can help train the system to make fewer mistakes. replies: Hello. welcome to google photos help community. If you've deleted an item and want to get it back, make sure it's in the trash. On your iPhone or iPad, open the Google Photos app . At the bottom, tap Library

>. Touch and hold the photo or video you want to restore. At the bottom, tap Restore . The photo or video will be back: In your phone’s gallery app In your Google Photos Account In any albums it was in If the item is not in your trash, it may have been permanently deleted. Check the archive and unarchive items On your iPhone or iPad, open the Google Photos app . Sign in to your Google Account. At the bottom, tap Library
> Archive . Select a photo. Touch and hold to select multiple photos. Tap More

> Unarchive . Don't see the photo or video? If a deleted photo or video isn't in trash, you can’t restore it. You won't be able to restore a photo if: You moved it to trash more than 60 days ago. You moved it to trash, then emptied your trash. You moved it to trash more than 30 days ago, and it wasn’t backed up. You permanently deleted it from your trash. You permanently deleted it from your device’s Gallery app, without backing it up first. For more information go to: <a href=

replies: Hi, Prashant Upadhyay 5837 Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum. Thanks for your post. Face recognition technology is evolving & can err. However, can you follow the steps below to remove the person from the current grouping & add that to another one? Tap to open the photo. Tap the three dots at the top right corner. Next, you will see a thumbnail of all the faces the app has identified, and a pencil icon. Once done, all the identified faces will display a minus sign at the top left corner of the thumbnail. Tap that. The thumbnail will now move down to the row of faces below, displaying the tag

. The minus sign will also change to a plus. Tap that plus. Now, the app will show the entire gallery of the persons identified to date. Then tap the matching suggestion. You can do this when editing is unavailable. Open the incorrectly identified photos > tap 3-dots > Remove results, and hope that Google will learn from it. But you should not remove them when both appear. You can also create a standard album for the unidentified faces, add the photos you want, and remove the wrong ones.

title: Google Photos People Face group tagging not working
text: I’m a relatively new user to Google photos, and while I did not have the face group feature enabled up until about a month ago, I did eventually follow the steps to enable it, and even after manually tagging a lot of photos, and taking a bunch since enabling it and doing that tagging, Google Photos is not going through any of my photos to tag these people in photos that they’re in historically. The only photos that exist under the people face groups are the ones that I manually tagged.

replies: Good day Steve! Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum! It is incredibly common for Google Photos to feel stuck when you first enable face grouping because the AI processing happens entirely on Google’s servers during idle time rather than on your computer or phone. Even though it has been a month, a large historical library can sometimes take weeks to be indexed, especially if the account hasn't been active enough to trigger a deep scan. You are essentially waiting in a digital queue, and historical photos are often processed with lower priority than newly uploaded ones. This is likely why only your manual tags are appearing; the automated scanner hasn't reached the

phase for your older media yet. The Album Kickstart Strategy One of the most effective ways to nudge the system into scanning your older photos is known as the Album Kickstart . The act of adding photos to a new album signals to Google's server that those specific files are high priority for the user. On the web interface, you should select a batch of around 500 older photos and add them to a new album. You do not need to keep this album forever, but leaving it for a few days often forces the AI to

those files, and you will frequently see faces from those specific photos begin to appear in the People section shortly after the server registers the change. Manual Triggers and Settings You can also try to jumpstart the algorithm by ensuring your own face is correctly labeled. Navigate to the People section, find your own face, and ensure it is tagged with the name

to a specific photo—such as adding a brief caption in the Info panel or applying a quick auto-color fix—forces Google to re-index that individual file immediately, which usually includes a fresh face scan. Interestingly, even toggling the

setting in your preferences can sometimes refresh the background scanning service for the entire library without disrupting your existing data. Crucial Warnings and Context Whatever you do, it is vital that you do not attempt to reset the feature by toggling the

setting off and then back on. While this feels like a logical troubleshooting step, doing so will permanently delete every manual tag you have spent the last month creating and will wipe all existing face models. This forces the entire process to start from zero and places your account at the very back of the processing queue again. Hope this helps. Regards, Lex

title: all my baby photos keep getting put in my oldest child's folder automatically
text: all my baby photos keep getting put in my oldest child's folder automatically instead of my baby's. they are showing up properly in my husband's photos though, which we share. but not on my login.

replies: Hi, Lucy Mantel Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum. Thanks for your post. Face recognition technology is evolving & can err. Also, there is no guarantee it will work correctly on every account, even when it does work correctly for one account. However, can you follow the steps below to remove the person from the current grouping & add that to another one? Tap to open the photo. Tap the three dots at the top right corner. Next, you will see a thumbnail of all the faces the app has identified, and a pencil icon. Once done, all identified faces will display a minus sign in the top-left corner of their thumbnails. Tap that. The thumbnail will now move down to the row of faces below, displaying the tag

. The minus sign will also change to a plus sign. Tap that plus. Now, the app will show the entire gallery of the persons identified to date. Tap the correct one & now the photo will be added to the proper grouping. You can tap the magnifying glass icon, start typing the name & narrow the search. Then tap the matching suggestion. You can do this when editing is unavailable. Open the incorrectly identified photos > tap 3-dots > Remove results, and hope that Google will learn from it. But you should not remove them when both appear. You can also create a standard album for the unidentified faces, add the photos you want, and remove the wrong ones.

title: Google Photos album lost 1,400+ videos and now my Custom order is gone
text: I have a Google Photos album with around 1,600 videos. At one point, around 1,400+ videos suddenly became invisible in the album. They were still in my main Google Photos library, and when I checked their Info, they still showed that they were in the album. I’ve had smaller versions of this happen before where the videos eventually came back, but this time it was over 1,400 videos. I shared the album with another Google account to see if that would fix it. When I opened the album on that account, all the videos were visible again and the original Custom order was still correct. I then unshared the other account. After that, the album on my original account started displaying the videos in Recently added order, even though the album still says Custom. This happens on both the website and the app. So my main question is: Is there any way to recover/reload the original Custom order? The fact that the correct Custom order was still visible on the shared album makes me think the original order may still exist somewhere. I really don’t want to delete/recreate the album or remove and re-add 1,600 videos because I spent a lot of time organizing them. I already submitted feedback through Google Photos, but I wanted to ask here in case anyone, especially a Product Expert, has seen this before or knows if the original Custom order can come back automatically.

replies: Hey! Be welcome to Googlee Photos Community! This is a known issue related to how Google Photos synchronizes custom sorting metadata for very large albums (especially those exceeding 1,000+ items). When a large portion of items temporarily disappears and then reappears, the local index/view of the album often gets disconnected from the backend custom order metadata. Because the second account displayed the custom order correctly, your custom ordering data is still intact on Google's servers —your primary account's session is simply stuck displaying a fallback cached view (

). Here is how you can try to force Google Photos to reload and re-sync the original custom order: Step 1: Force a Re-Sync via Sharing Settings Since sharing previously forced the backend to render the full album on the second account, re-establishing a shared view is the most reliable way to pull the correct custom order metadata back to your primary account: Open the album on photos.google.com on a desktop browser. Click the Share button at the top right and share it again with a second Google account (or create a shareable link). Log into that second account (preferably in an Incognito / Private browser window ) and open the album. Verify if the Custom order is correctly displayed on the second account. While viewing the album on the second account, click Edit album or change the sort s

view: Web Browser: Clear your browser cache and cookies for photos.google.com , or test viewing the album in an Incognito window. Mobile App (Android): Long-press the Google Photos app icon > App info > Storage & cache > Clear cache . (Do not tap

if you have unsynced items or Locked Folder files). Why This Happens Google Photos relies on database indexers to maintain custom sorting positions. In albums with over 1,000–1,500 items, temporary server-side index drops can cause the UI to fall back to default chronological sorting even though the custom index array exists on the backend. Toggling the sorting properties or viewing it through a shared instance forces the server to regenerate the view index. I hope had been helpful! Let us knoe if this is a good answer marking 👍

or shuffle the photos. Missing or Mixed Metadata Timestamps: Google Photos automatically sorts items by EXIF metadata (Date & Time taken). title: I lost all the face I named even mine
text: I've lost all the collections i groupd by face even mine as well & now when I try to add a name label again it says couldn't add face try again

replies: Good day Me 3004! Welcome to the Google Photos Community Support Forum! This issue happens when Google's server-side face grouping index becomes temporarily glitched, locked, or desynced from your Android device. The error message

appears because your local app is trying to write a label to a face-cluster database on Google's cloud servers that is currently locked or mid-reset. Step 1: Check Your Face Groups via a Browser First, verify whether your face collections are still intact on Google's cloud servers or if they vanished globally: Open a browser on a phone or computer and go to <a href=

>photos.google.com/people . Sign into the same Google Account. Check if your face groups and name labels still exist here. If your named faces appear on the web: Your cloud data is completely safe, and the issue is simply a temporary sync glitch inside the mobile app on your phone. Proceed to Step 2 . If the page is empty on the web: Your face index was recently reset on the server. Jump to Step 3 . Step 2: Fix the App Sync Glitch (Clear Cache & Unrestrict Battery) If your app's session token is corrupted, clearing the temporary app cache forces Google Photos to re-download your face database from the cloud: On your Android phone, go to Settings --> Apps --> Photos . Tap Force Stop . Tap Storage & cache --> tap Clear cache . (Do NOT tap

) . Go back one screen, tap Battery (or App battery usage ), and set it to Unrestricted . (This prevents Android from killing the background face-sync process). Re-open Google Photos, tap Collections --> People & pets , and wait a few minutes for the face circles to repopulate. Step 3: Trigger a Server Re-Scan (If Face Grouping Was Reset) If face grouping was toggled off recently—or if Google's background index reset itself—the system must re-scan your photo library before allowing you to add new name labels. Do Not Toggle Settings Off and On Do not turn the
setting OFF and ON in your settings. Toggling it OFF will permanently wipe your entire cloud face database, forcing a complete restart of the indexing queue. To clear the

error and allow the server to re-index your faces: Open Google Photos --> tap your Profile Icon --> Photos settings . Tap Preferences --> Group similar faces . Ensure Face grouping is turned ON . Plug your phone into a charger, connect to Wi-Fi , and leave the phone idle overnight. Once the background server finishes registering your library's face embeddings, the error will vanish, and your existing face groups (or the ability to create new name labels) will automatically restore. Hope this helps. Regards, Lex

Hello CPolarBear, Just to clarify, Google Photos doesn’t create, delete, or manage folders on your phone in the same way your device’s file manager does. It can read and display the photos and videos inside your device folders, and if backup is enabled, those items can be backed up to your Google Photos library. Google Photos doesn’t automatically back up your device folders as separate albums with the same folder names, so photos stored in different folders on your phone may all appear together in the main Google Photos library after backup. You need to reorganize them into albums again. To make it easier, you can try searching by date, location, people, or keywords instead of going through everything manually. Usually, photos from the same folder are uploaded or shown close together in o

It may also be related to the Free up space feature. If the backedup photos were removed from the device, the local folders may become empty, and your phone’s file manager may no longer show them or treat them as photo folders. Hope this helps clarify what may have happened. Rahmat

text: Are all the photos not at one location? Is the face recognition not working properly? Hasn't Moments or much else been updated either?

replies: Google Photos frequently processes and updates its AI features behind the scenes, but this can sometimes lead to issues with location tracking, facial recognition syncing, or delayed Memories. Location Tracking Your photos may not be tied to one location for a few specific reasons: Missing Camera Data: Photos will only show up in their correct location on the map if your camera app had

enabled at the time the picture was taken. Location Estimations: For photos taken on cameras without GPS, Google Photos attempts to estimate where the picture was taken based on nearby landmarks or locations in your other photos. Check Settings: To ensure missing locations are being estimated, go to your Photos app ( rightarrow ) Settings ( rightarrow ) Privacy ( rightarrow ) Location Options and make sure Estimate missing locations is toggled on. Face Recognition If your facial recognition isn't working properly, it could be due to a known temporary bug, poor image lighting, or a cache glitch. To fix it: Toggle Face Groups: Go to Settings ( rightarrow ) Privacy ( rightarrow ) Face Groups. Toggle it off, wait a few minutes, and turn it back on to force a re-scan of your library. Check the
and Other Features Google Photos has received several recent updates rather than remaining stagnant: Memory Highlights:

are constantly updated and surfaced as personalized Memories . For the end of the year, the app generates a highly personalized Recap to highlight your year in photos and stats. Search Changes: You can now toggle between classic keyword searches and Ask Photos (an AI-powered search for complex queries). Editing Updates: Google has introduced subtle AI-driven Touch-Up tools that let you smooth out or brighten faces directly in the image editor. Face Thumbnails: The mobile app has introduced a new feature that tests putting face detection thumbnails directly below your photos, making it easier to see who Google has identified. This way, one photo of a sunset with a loved one could appear in a sunset album, a loved one album, a vacation album, etc. So to answer your original question 1. select a photo or group of photos from the main view 2. add them to an album 3. return to the main view 4. select the same images again 5. select archive the images. They will remove from the main view, but still show in albums and in search, etc. Continue down the line, adding to albums and then archiving the images. At the end, your main view will be empty and you'l
>blog resources here for Photos. There are a lot of options for organizing your images, so enjoy the process! Go slow to avoid errors, take breaks as it can get overwhelming at first.

title: Locked folder not opening.
text: Locked folder

replies: Hello, Welcome to the Google Photos Help Community. Please note: Photos stored in the Locked Folder are permanently deleted once removed. They do not move to the Trash and cannot be recovered. The Locked Folder is device-specific, meaning items are saved only on your device and are not backed up to Google Photos unless you manually enable backup for the Locked Folder. You may lose Locked Folder items that aren’t backed up if: • You uninstall or clear data from the Google Photos app • You uninstall app updates • Your device is lost, damaged, or factory reset • You switch devices without transferring your data Once photos or videos are deleted from the Locked Folder, they are permanently erased from your device and any associated backup. 👉 To prevent loss, always save a copy of important ite

title: I can't find the rest of my downloads.
text: Can you please recover them

replies: Open the built-in Files by Google app (or your device's file manager) and tap on Downloads to see if the files are still listed there. Navigate to Internal Storage > Download to check if the files were moved or hidden. If the missing items are photos, open Google Photos , go to Library > Trash , and check if they were accidentally deleted within the last 60 days. Please let me know clearly about your queries. title: All my Google Photos data is missing from my account. I have checked Trash/Bin, Archive, and the cor
text: My Google Photos data has disappeared from my account. I am using the correct Google account, but my photos and videos are not visible in Google Photos. I have already tried these steps: 1. Checked Trash/Bin, but the data is not there. 2. Checked Archive, but photos/videos are not visible. 3. Checked Google Photos website. 4. Checked other Google accounts on my phone. 5. Checked device folders in Google Photos. I did not want to permanently delete my photos/videos. Please review my Google Photos account and help me recover the missing photos and videos if recovery is possible.

replies: Hello User Welcome to the Google Photos Help Community. You can only restore photos and videos if they’re still in your trash. Unfortunately, Once photos are permanently deleted from the Trash/Bin in Google Photos, they cannot be recovered. This action is irreversible, as items removed from the trash are permanently erased from Google's servers. While it's not possible to restore these files, you can learn more about how the deletion process works and how to recover recently deleted photos by checking out the official Google Support article:<a href=

> Recovering deleted photos and videos . It's a tough situation, but I hope this information clarifies things for you. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask. With regards, Md Papel Mahammud Hope this helps. If helpful, please hit 👍and recommend.
